Stockton CA, Estados Unidos (1989 – 1999, 2010 –)
Pavement se formó en 1989 como un proyecto de los guitarristas y vocalistas Stephen Malkmus y Scott Kannberg. Sus primeros EP’s tuvieron un estilo lo-fi (Slay Tracks (1933-1969), Demolition Plot J-7, and Perfect Sound Forever) y fueron grabados en «Louder Than You Think», el estudio del que sería el nuevo miembro, el excéntrico Gary Young (batería).

scenes.name: Lo-fi pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El gran invento de los independientes neozelandeses se convierte en uno de los fenómenos mundiales de los noventa: Cakekitchen, Bailter Space, Underground Lovers, King Loser; en Australia, Blackeyed Susans y Moles. En EE UU, Olympia (Beat Happening, Some Velvet Sidewalk, Spinanes), Modest Mouse y, sobre todo, Pavement, el grupo lo-fi más influyente (Slanted And Enchanted), con su contagio por todo el país (Silver Jews, Crowsdell). La vertiente más creativa, heredera de Half Japanese y los Residents: Trumans Water, Velocity Girl, Heavy Vegetable, Quintron, Danielson Famile, Soul Junk.

podcast.title: Influence on Damon Albarn (1997)
podcast.body: Pavement was one of the low-fi American alternative bands that fascinated Damon Albarn of Blur by 1997, contributing to his "stunning aesthetic reversal" away from Britpop and towards new sonic explorations. "Damon had become fascinated by low-fi American alternative music from bands like Pavement."

podcast.title: Nearly Ten-Year Hiatus (2009)
podcast.body: Pavement's last show was on November 20, 1999, and their reunion was announced on September 15, 2009, indicating a hiatus that was two months short of 10 years. "Pavements last show, November 20th, 1999, a reunion was announced on September 15th, 2009. So that's two months short of 10 years."

podcast.title: Direct Inspiration from R.E.M.
podcast.body: Pavement is noted as one of the major American alternative rock bands of the 1990s whose members were directly influenced by R.E.M., even attending their concerts. Pavement's formation in the late 1980s, concurrent with R.E.M.'s rising success, indicates the direct lineage of inspiration for the burgeoning Californian alternative rock scene. "miembros de Payment, por ejemplo, iban a los conciertos S&M."

podcast.title: Lofi Influence on Later Bands
podcast.body: Pavement's unique Lofi approach had a significant influence on later bands, with their sound being heard in the music of late 90s Blur, as well as groups like Modest Mouse, Spoon, and The Walkmen. "Pavement's influence would later be heard in the music of late 90s blur, and also groups like Modest Mouse, Spoon, and The Walkman."

podcast.title: Stockton, California Origins
podcast.body: Pavement was described as a four-piece band from Stockton, California, known for specializing in a straightforward, sometimes woozy form of distorted indie guitar rock that became emblematic of the Lofi sound of the 1990s. "A great example of the kind of Lofi that vaulted forward in the 90s came from pavement, a four piece from Stockton, California that specialized in straightforward, sometimes woozy forms of distorted indie guitar rock."

xref.title: Fractured Skull Attack (August 1983) – Street Brawl Led to Brain Surgery, Later Distrust of Doctors, and Death
xref.body: In August 1983, Johnny Ramone became involved in a brawl with Seth Maclin of a band called Sub Zero Construction on the street outside Johnny's East Village apartment at 4am. Johnny was beaten to the pavement and kicked in the head. He was rushed to hospital with a fractured skull and required brain surgery. He recovered, but the incident left him deeply distrustful of doctors. When he later began experiencing abdominal pain — roughly 15 years after the attack — his mistrust caused him to delay seeking treatment. The abdominal pain was aggressive prostate cancer that spread throughout his body. Chemotherapy failed, and Johnny died on September 15, 2004. "Had he not been beaten up in the summer of 1983 and still trusted doctors?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Vehicular Manslaughter of Razzle (1984)
xref.body: In 1984, Vince Neil and Razzle, the drummer for Hanoi Rocks, left a party in Neil's powerful 1972 Ford Pantera to get more alcohol. While driving 65 mph in a 25 mph zone, Neil hit a wet patch, crossed into oncoming traffic, and crashed into two cars. Razzle died in the hospital, and Neil suffered cuts and cracked ribs. "While going 65 in a 25 miles per hour zone, the Pantera hit a wet patch of pavement, it crossed over into the opposite lane and crashed into two cars traveling the other way."

xref.title: Lollapalooza "Party in a Bottle" Incident (1992)
xref.body: Backstage at Lollapalooza in 1992, Al Jourgensen forced someone to drink from a bottle of Bushmills whiskey with a broken, jagged neck, threatening physical harm if they refused. It was later revealed that Jourgensen was known to add a "dollop of acid" to his Bushmills, creating what he referred to as a "party in a bottle," though this particular addition fortunately did not occur that day. "I ended up backstage with Al at Lala Paloza in 1992 and he made me drink from a bottle of bush mill whiskey that had dropped on the pavement."

xref.title: Origin of Sergeant Pepper Mustaches
xref.body: In late 1966, all members of The Beatles began growing mustaches, a fashion choice prominently featured on the artwork for their "Sergeant Pepper" album the following year. This trend originated after Paul McCartney had a moped crash, resulting in a face injury and a scar on his lip from bad stitches. He grew a mustache to conceal the scar, and the rest of the band followed suit. "Paul McCarty had a crash on a moat pad, which resulted in a faceplant on the pavement and this left a scar on his lip due to some bad stitches. And he became self-conscious of the scar. He grew a mustache and the rest of the band followed."
